description: Scenario B. Deterministic high-motion GPU workload rendered by Superposition Benchmark 1.1 Pro on the primary 2560x1440@144 display, captured by ExoSnap while the application itself stays visible on the secondary display. Calibrated for headroom, NOT for maximum GPU load: the question is what the frontend costs under a demanding real-time workload, not how fast the RTX 5070 Ti is.
source_notes: Superposition Benchmark 1.1 Pro, DirectX, 2560x1440, borderless fullscreen, DoF/motion blur/sound off. No frame generation (Superposition predates it).

workload.calibration_note: Scene 8 chosen from a measured survey of scenes 0/3/5/8/11/14/17 plus the default sequence, each for one minute at 1440p High (.workspace/benchmark-results/calibration/scene-survey/survey.json). Every candidate sits at the 144 Hz vsync cap; scene 8 is the ONLY one whose mean falls meaningfully below it (138.7 vs 142.8 fps) and it carries by far the highest frame-to-frame variability (4.88 vs 2.7-4.2). The others are indistinguishable precisely because they idle against vsync, where added ExoSnap load could not become visible. GPU utilisation 71.8% mean / 75% p95 and 63 degC peak confirm headroom rather than saturation, which is what this scenario is calibrated for -- Extreme quality would turn it into a GPU-starvation test and belongs in a separately named saturated scenario. Corroborating: loop_scene_8_high_5min.xml is one of Unigine's own documented sample routines. FROZEN: do not change between Widgets and Quick runs.

settings_rationale: The shipped default profile for screen capture: MKV + AV1 + Opus, CFR 60 fps, 4:2:0, 8-bit, SDR, SYS on / MIC off. Superposition itself runs with -sound 0, so SYS carries silence — the audio thread, the mux and the A/V clock slaving are still exercised, which is what makes the run production-like. 60 fps from a 144 Hz source deliberately produces CFR coalescing; that is what the shipped default does on this machine, and the pressure is identical on both frontends.
